questions.q: Which type of model is LEAST affected by feature scaling?
questions.explain: Trees only ask whether a value is above a threshold, so multiplying or shifting a column does not change their splits.

questions.q: What does StandardScaler do to each column?
options: Subtracts the mean and divides by the standard deviation
Squeezes values into the range 0 to 1
questions.explain: Standardization gives each column mean 0 and standard deviation 1 (a z-score).

questions.q: Where should a scaler be fitted?
options: On the whole dataset before splitting
On the test set, so it matches new data
On the training set only, then used to transform train, validation and test
questions.explain: Fitting on all data leaks test statistics into training. Fit on the training set only, then reuse those statistics everywhere.

questions.q: In the wine example, scaling raised kNN accuracy from about 72% to 96%. Why did kNN benefit so much?
options: kNN cannot read unscaled numbers at all
Scaling adds new information to the data
Proline, with a huge numeric range, was dominating the distance calculation until scaling gave every feature a fair say
questions.explain: kNN is distance-based, and a feature with a big numeric range dominated the distances. Scaling equalized the influence.

questions.q: Your column has a few extreme outliers you have decided to keep. Which scaler is the most suitable?
questions.explain: RobustScaler uses the median and interquartile range, so outliers barely affect the scale, whereas min-max and standard scaling get stretched by them.
